evidence.note: Detected a falsified decoding-representation assumption: SIMD memory ops collided in MemOp/SimdOp and SimdOp variants lacked MemArg; reworked types.rs to carry MemArg — a genuine design correction.

After macros repeatedly failed to compile in match-arm position, abandoned the macro approach and inlined exec_numeric, and used a minimal runtime.rs to isolate which files compiled — a real approach shift, though mostly compilation-level rather than semantic.

Strongest correction: recognized SIMD sub-opcode numbers were arbitrarily (wrongly) assigned and regenerated decode.rs with official 0x00-0xE8 numbers, noting exec_simd is decode-order-independent — fixing the generator of decode failures once (anchor-8 flavor).
The opcode fix left SIMD pass rate unchanged at 240/445; the agent observed this but never re-diagnosed why, leaving a falsified assumption uncorrected.
validate_module patch failed to fix the 83 assert_invalid failures; agent rationalized it as possibly unnecessary rather than reworking the root cause.
~150 steps repeating identical terminal-recovery attempts (Ctrl+C/kill/pkill/exec/reset/stty) without revising the theory — sustained circular re-debugging, the anti-pattern of anchor 0.

reasoning: The agent shows one clear root-cause structural correction (the arbitrary→official SIMD opcode-number rework at 123-124) plus a couple of smaller approach shifts (MemArg restructure, abandoning macros), which lifts it above pure local-patching. But the whole horizon is dominated by failures to course-correct: the opcode fix produced no improvement yet was never re-diagnosed, the validation patch was rationalized instead of reworked, and roughly half the trajectory is an endless loop of identical failed terminal-recovery attempts — textbook circular re-debugging. That mix of one solid mid-level correction against a large body of un-revisited, repeated failure lands it at a 4, between the local-patching anchors (0-3) and the consistent step-back-and-reconsider behavior of anchor 5.
